issues.detail: The Hebrew 'גֵּאֶה' means 'proud/arrogant' (person), not '山岡' (mountain/hill). The Chinese mistranslates the object of the verb.

The Hebrew imperative 'הַכְנִיעֵהוּ' ('subdue him') is a command addressed to someone (likely Job), but the Chinese renders it as first-person past/future '我已使...降卑' ('I have made...humble'), changing the subject and tense.

The Hebrew 'וַהֲדֹךְ רְשָׁעִים תַּחְתָּם' ('and tread down the wicked in their place') is rendered as '並要將惡人踐踏在他們以下' which is close, but the first clause's imperative force is lost; also 'תַּחְתָּם' ('in their place/under them') is rendered as '在他們以下' which is acceptable, but the main issue is the first clause.
